findings.title: The known-red window misses every scripted-pair test that breaks when master's gunner sends laserLock to the laser-less Hound (Task 3 to Task 8)
findings.claim: From Task 3 on, the Cutter has no laser, but the scripted gunner is still master's code until Task 8. On master the gunner pushes `laserLock` whenever the target is seen and `!sys.laserTargeted`, which is every tick on a laser-less class. The step answers each one `unavailable`. So any test that requires every scripted command to be applied goes red, and those tests are not in the window. The window lists only the goldens, a few trajectory pins and 'duelScripted's whole-run values'. Task 3 Step 10's fallout rule has no class for these: they are not ports, not kind (a) without an owner, and not kind (b). Step 10 also defers any kind (b) pin found in another file to Task 14, which contradicts 'only these'.
findings.evidence: scripted.ts:L340-L341 (`if (!sys.laserTargeted || sys.lock !== want) out.push({ kind: 'laserLock' ...})`); state.ts:L227 (laserTargeted = crew && laser !== null, so false on the Hound); step.ts:L313 (laserLock is `unavailable` with a null laser); tests/helpers/scriptedDuel.ts:L39-L46, L55 (requireApplied throws on any non-applied scripted command); tests/duelOracle.test.ts:L89-L90 (`runDuel(1, 'scripted', 1300, 600)`); tests/duelScripted.test.ts:L69-L87 (the repair-walk test asserts every result is 'applied' over 900 ticks). Plan L62-L65 (the window), L508 (Step 10), L1258-L1436 (Task 8 fixes the gunner).
findings.why: The plan's binding rule is that every test not in the window passes at the end of each task. Executors at Tasks 3-7 will find red tests that no rule covers, and two executors will handle them differently (one tunes, one skips, one stops).
findings.fix: Recommended: in Task 3, add the one-line guard at the top of `gunner`: `if (hasTurret(classOf(d.tactical, 0))) { /* W-4a: Task 8 builds houndGunner */ pair.barMoved = true; return; }`, then have Task 8 replace it with `houndGunner`. Alternatively, extend the window by name: all of `tests/duelOracle.test.ts` and `tests/duelScripted.test.ts`, the `runDuel`-based cases of `tests/engWeapons.test.ts`, and any `requireApplied` or all-applied scripted test. Make them red from Task 3 until Task 8, with Task 8 Step 5 running them. Also say explicitly that a kind (b) pin found in Step 10 joins the window until Task 14.

findings.title: Task 7 won't type-check: duelScripted's `pewAimOf` reads `c.aim` / `c.aimAcc` on the new `{ kind: 'pewFire' }`
findings.claim: Task 7 changes `DuelCommand`'s pewFire member to `{ kind: 'pewFire' }`. `tests/duelScripted.test.ts`'s `pewAimOf` reads `c.aim * 256 + c.aimAcc` after narrowing on `c.kind === 'pewFire'`, which becomes a compile error. Task 7 Step 6's grep (`kind: 'pewFire'`) misses this line, and the plan defers duelScripted to Task 8. `tsc -b` includes `tests/**`, so Task 7 Step 7's 'tsc clean' fails.
findings.evidence: tests/duelScripted.test.ts:L118-L124 (`return c && c.kind === 'pewFire' ? c.aim * 256 + c.aimAcc : -1;`); tsconfig.web.json:L10 (include has `tests/**/*`); plan L1147-L1150 (the new pewFire member), L1242 (the grep), L1246-L1247 (tsc clean expected), L1270 (Task 8 replaces pewAimOf).
findings.why: Task 7 can't finish as written: tsc is red and the task's commit gate fails.
findings.fix: In Task 7 Step 6, grep `'pewFire'` (not `kind: 'pewFire'`) across `tests/`. Either replace `pewAimOf` there with Task 8's `pewFires` helper (plan L1273-L1278), or delete the W-1 gunnerPew describe block in Task 7 and leave only the new block to Task 8.

findings.title: Task 9 won't type-check: `KeyAction` gains selectPrev / selectNext, but controlsList's exhaustive `DUEL_ACTION` record is only updated in Task 12
findings.claim: `DUEL_ACTION` is typed `Record<Exclude<KeyAction, 'fireUp'>, string>`. Adding `'selectPrev' | 'selectNext'` to `KeyAction` in Task 9 makes that literal miss two required keys. Task 9's file list does not include `app/controlsList.ts`, yet Task 9 Step 9 expects tsc to be clean. The entries and the loop's `continue` arrive only in Task 12 Step 5.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/app/controlsList.ts:L19-L36 (the exhaustive Record), L47-L50 (the loop over every action); plan L1449-L1454 (Task 9 files), L1611 (KeyAction gains them), L1771-L1772 (tsc clean expected), L2157-L2158 (Task 12 adds them).
findings.fix: Move to Task 9 (and add controlsList.ts to its Files) the `DUEL_ACTION` entries `selectPrev` / `selectNext` and the `continue` for them in the loop. Leave the merged rows and the text changes to Task 12.

findings.title: Task 11's online branch calls `requests.triggerHeld()` on the ContactRequests, not the MapRequests
findings.claim: Inside `play`, `requests` is the `ContactRequests` parameter. Inside `pump`, `requests` is shadowed by `contact.takeRequests()`. Neither has `triggerHeld`, so both new calls fail to compile. The file already warns about this shadowing and works around it with closures (`takeSteer0`, `pewRequest`).
findings.evidence: onlineDuel.ts:L98 (`requests = createMapRequests()`), L120-L122 (the shadowing comment and `takeSteer0`), L233 (`play(..., requests: ContactRequests, ...)`), L357 (`const requests = contact.takeRequests()` in pump); plan L2037 (`const trig = requests.triggerHeld();` in play), L2049 (`trigger: requests.triggerHeld()` in pump).
findings.why: tsc fails in Task 11, and the online trigger can't be read as written.
findings.fix: Add `const triggerNow = (): boolean => requests.triggerHeld();   // W-4: the map's trigger, read through a closure as takeSteer0` beside L122. Use `triggerNow()` in the Hound branch of `play` and in `pump`'s `sessionHeld(..., { sel: weaponSel, trigger: triggerNow() })`.

findings.title: Task 5's 'a static rock wakes on the push' test can't pass: a Static rock written into a free slot isn't in the broad-phase grid
findings.claim: `rocksNear` finds Static rocks only through `queryGrid(s.grid, …)`, and that grid is built once from the map's asteroids at their seeded positions. Moving rocks are scanned by position. The test writes `RockKind.Static` into slot 100 at (200, −2500). The round's sweep never sees it, so there is no push, the rock stays Static and the assertion fails. The arena also clears every rock.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/rocks.ts:L60-L72 (Static via queryGrid, Moving via scan); state.ts:L281 (`grid: buildGrid(map.asteroids, map.rMap)`); tests/helpers/rockArena.ts:L9-L18 (arena empties the pool), L23-L27 (`seeded(st, k)`: 'the grid indexes it there'); plan L738-L743 (the test).
findings.why: The test is red after the implementation is correct, with no rule to fix it.
findings.fix: Use `seeded(st, k)` for a map asteroid k, then fire the round at `st.map.asteroids[k]` from `a.x - a.r - 5` along +x, and assert `st.rocks[k * ROCK_STRIDE] === RockKind.Moving` and `rockAt(st, k).vx > 0`.

findings.title: Task 13's observer reads `systems.0.weaponPower.${k}`, which no field is named; weaponPower is one 3-wide vector
findings.claim: `flattenTactical` registers weaponPower as `vector('systems.${i}.weaponPower', WEAPON_SLOTS, …)`. The observer's `named()` maps each field name to the offset of its first value. So `n.at.get('systems.0.weaponPower.1')` is undefined, `powered[*].weaponPower[1]` is undefined, and the smoke's `until(... === 1)` times out. The plan's 'check the names' hedge leaves the right form to the executor.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/hash.ts:L132 (`vector(`systems.${i}.weaponPower`, WEAPON_SLOTS, …)`); scripts/network/duel-app-observer.ts:L16-L24 (`at.set(f.name, k); k += f.count`), L55; plan L2198 (the key), L2216 (the until).
findings.why: `npm run test:duel-app-runtime` fails in Task 13 and again in Task 14 Step 4.
findings.fix: State it exactly: `const wp = n.at.get('systems.0.weaponPower')!;` then `weaponPower: [0, 1, 2].map((k) => v[wp + k]!)`. The scalars `systems.0.pewShots`, `systems.0.gunShots` and `systems.0.missilesLaunched` are correct as written (hash.ts:L24-L26 SYSTEMS_TAIL). Drop the hedge.

findings.title: Resolve the items left to the executor; each has a definite answer in the code
findings.claim:
Several steps say 'check and adjust' where the code already gives one answer, so they should state it:
- Task 3: the validator is `validateTacticalValues(shape, values, offset = 0)`, but the plan calls it with (values, shape).
- Task 5: the `fx` cast should be the real constructor.
- Tasks 6 and 7: the noop hedge is unnecessary; their expectations are already right.
- Task 12: render may import app.
- Task 11: folding the AUTO F launch into one `refusal` check differs from today's code, which sends an AUTO launch only when the replica's `canLaunch` holds, and the plan asks the executor to align it.
findings.evidence: hash.ts:L283 (`validateTacticalValues(shape: TacticalState, values: ArrayLike<number>, offset = 0)`), L288 (the error names the field, so /gunCooldown/ matches); render/tactical/fxModel.ts:L57 (`createFx()`), tests/rockFx.test.ts:L42 (`const hit = createFx(); pushRockFx(hit, …)`); step.ts:L272-L273 and net/contracts.ts:L142 (a noop is `{ id, tick, status: 'noop' }` with an optional reason); render/duel/consoleModel.ts:L3-L4 (render already imports app/duel/controls and app/duel/input); onlineDuel.ts:L331-L338 (today's MANUAL/AUTO F split); plan L339, L811, L980, L2132, L2045.
findings.why: These are the 'left to check at execution' defects the brief names. The F-handling one could be built two ways online.
findings.fix:
Write the answers into the plan:
- Task 3: `validateTacticalValues(st, flattenTactical(st))`.
- Task 5: `const fx = createFx()` from `../src/renderer/src/render/tactical/fxModel`, then assert `fx.items.map((i) => i.kind)` equals `['spark']`. Also state the planet tie as written (a Moving rock is found by radius, rocks.ts:L64-L69, so the same circle gives the same t).
- Tasks 6 and 7: drop the noop hedge.
- Task 12: import `autocannonRateText` from `../../app/duel/weaponsSeat` directly.
- Task 11: keep today's two branches verbatim: `if (launches > 0 && torpManual) {…torpSent…} else if (launches > 0 && canLaunch(d.tactical, 0, sys0.torpRock, false)) send({ kind: 'missileLaunch' })`, plus the AUTO `refusal` line as at L340-L342.

findings.title: Key-path ports leave tests red between tasks: valkyrnRuntime from Task 9, and scienceInput's Weapons-frequency case from Task 3
findings.claim:
Two between-task reds that the plan doesn't list:
- **valkyrnRuntime (Task 9):** Task 9 Step 8 switches valkyrnRuntime to `hold({ freqKeyTo: 1 })`, but the runtime reads `k.freqTo` until Task 10's `laserFreqKey`. Its NO LASER and laser-fit tune cases are red at the end of Task 9. The plan admits this ('goes green in Task 10') but doesn't list it in the window.
- **scienceInput (Tasks 3 to 5):** the 'Weapons: 3/4/5 (or a button) send laserFrequency' case runs on the default class (the Hound). From Task 3 until Task 6, `laserFrequency` is `unavailable` on a class with no laser, so that case is red. Task 2's table files scienceInput as 'kind (a), Task 9', not as a port.
- **No laser-fit port needed:** Task 9 Step 8's 'if that runtime is the Hound, port it to the laser fit' is unnecessary. `gunFreqRequest` falls back on `freqTo`, so the console-button case stays valid on the Hound once Task 6 admits it.
findings.evidence: tests/valkyrnRuntime.test.ts:L127-L143; tests/scienceInput.test.ts:L64-L83 (rig: default cls, `freq` sets freqTo), L124-L133; step.ts:L387 (laserFrequency `unavailable` without a laser until Task 6); plan L62-L65, L249, L1765-L1767, L1772, L1756 (`gunFreqRequest` = `gunFreqKeyTo ?? freqTo`).
findings.why: The 'every other test passes at the end of each task' rule is broken twice, and Task 9 Step 9 expects scienceInput to pass.
findings.fix: Move the valkyrnRuntime `freqTo` → `freqKeyTo` edit (spec §9 L486) into Task 10, beside the `laserFreqKey` edit. Either list `scienceInput.test.ts` L124-L133 in the window from Task 3 to Task 6, or move Task 6's admission change into Task 3. In Task 9 Step 8, state that the scienceInput runtime case keeps `freqTo` (the button) and stays on the Hound.

findings.title: Spec §14's loadout test 'every laser command from the Hound except laserFrequency is unavailable' has no task
findings.claim: `w4Loadout.test.ts` checks the defs, the start power, the trim and the bound, but it never steps a duel. No other W-4a test sends `laserLock`, `laserCharge`, `laserMode`, `laserFire` or `rockLock {weapon: 'laser'}` from the Hound's Weapons seat and expects `unavailable`. Task 6 covers only `laserFrequency`'s admission.
findings.evidence: spec L699-L705 (the Loadout bullets); plan L291-L336 (w4Loadout as written), L961-L976 (Task 6's laserFrequency case only); step.ts:L313 (the rule under test).
findings.why: This is a spec requirement in W-4a's scope with no test. It pins the Hound side of the no-laser rule that the beam ports moved off the Cutter.
findings.fix: Add a case to `tests/w4PewFire.test.ts` (it already has the duel envelope helper). On `createSeatedDuel(CUTTER, 5)`, the gunner sends `laserLock {room: 1}`, `laserCharge {held: true}`, `laserMode {manual: true}`, `laserFire {aim: 0, aimAcc: 0}` and `rockLock {weapon: 'laser', rock: -1}` in one tick. Expect every result `rejected` / `unavailable`, then `laserFrequency {freq: 1}` `applied`.

findings.title: The test bodies for Tasks 10, 11 and 12 are titles and comments, not tests
findings.claim: Task 10's `w4Runtime.test.ts` and Task 12's UI `it` blocks are empty bodies or comment sketches. Task 11 asks for three session cases 'in the idiom of' another file. These carry the riskiest app paths: the held trigger's press edge, W/S refusing with the command still queued, 3 not tuning, the laser fit keeping Space/Z/3, and the online held-change stamp. The rigs they should copy exist and are short enough to name.
findings.evidence: plan L1802-L1818, L1973, L2086-L2104; the rigs: tests/scienceInput.test.ts:L65-L83 (a compact runtime rig with sampleKeys/scheduler/contact), tests/valkyrnRuntime.test.ts:L127-L143 (`rig({ cls })`, `hold`, `takeRefusals`), tests/duelRuntime.test.ts (`rt`), tests/manualTorpedoUi.test.tsx (makeUi).
findings.why: Two executors will write different tests, and a weak one can pass a broken branch. One example: `deps.triggerHeld` is read only on the press edge with the autocannon selected, which is easy to under-test.
findings.fix: Write at least the runtime file in full on the scienceInput `rig()` pattern, with `triggerHeld` and `takePew` deps, asserting `rt.held()[me]` and `rt.lastResults()` / `rt.takeRefusals()`. For the UI and online cases, name the exact rig (file and function) and the exact selector or value each assertion reads.

findings.title: Task 2 moves every arena-based rock test onto the laser fit, not just the beam's
findings.claim: Changing `arena`'s default class to `ShipClass.ValkyrnLaser` moves 10 rock test files onto FIGHTER flight and VALKYRN_HULL, including rockShips, rockContacts, rockBlast, rockBreak and manualTorpedoMode, whose subject isn't the beam. Most read hull deltas, so they likely still pass. But the port rule (plan L58) is for 'a test of the crew beam's own rules'.
findings.evidence: plan L229-L233; tests/helpers/rockArena.ts:L11-L18; arena( is used in rockBlast, rockBreak, rockContacts, rockShips, rockFx, rockTargetModel, rockMaskBetweenTicks, manualTorpedoMode and engineeringFog, besides rockLaser.
